text:
This is my usual setup. Give it a try if you’d like! 

I'm using a Sony ZV-E1 mounted on a DJI Ronin RS2 (SuperSmooth mode) with Pan-Tilt Fast and Lens Support.
Settings:
• S-Log3 (+1.7 EV)
• 4K 10-bit 4:2:2
• 60fps / Shutter Speed 1/100 (to reduce flickering)
• WB: 3500K
Post-processing:
• Stabilized with Gyroflow or Catalyst Browse.
• Edited in Final Cut Pro.
• Color graded using S-Log3 LUT with minor adjustments based on my mood.
Important Setup Tips:
• Camera Choice: It’s best to use a camera that can record gyro data internally for precise stabilization in post.
• Stabilization: This is crucial—turn OFF the in-camera stabilization (IBIS) since we’re using Gyroflow/Catalyst Browse in post.
• Processing Time: Keep in mind that stabilization takes a lot of time and power. For a 1-hour video, it takes about 6 hours to process. You'll need a high-performance PC for this.
• Heat Management: Since the ZV-E1 can overheat, I use the Ulanzi CU01 Thermostatic Semiconductor Camera Cooler Kit. I run it in Auto Mode using USB power instead of a battery pack. I also set the camera's "Auto Power Off Temp" to High.
• Reflections: To prevent dashboard reflections, you should lay down some black wool paper or fabric. I use Musou Black Fabric Kiwami (https://ansoken.black/products/musou-black-fabric-kiwami?variant=48994267234611).
• Mounting: As for mounting the gimbal, you'll need to get creative depending on your car—I secure mine to a heavy-duty tripod.
• ISO & Lens: I set the ISO to 12,800 to take advantage of the dual base ISO. Make sure to use a camera with dual base ISO and a fast lens (f/2.8 or brighter).
With this setup, you can capture the exact same look as mine!

Also, a tip for the best quality: shooting on a clear night without clouds makes the blacks deeper and much more beautiful.

Hope this helps your setup!
